title: Korean Fried Chicken Wings with Gochujang Glaze
summary: Whole chicken wings cured overnight with salt, MSG and ginger, coated in a potato-starch batter and dredge, double-fried and tossed in a sweet, tangy gochujang-garlic sauce.
notes: Video: 'The Best Korean Fried Chicken At Home' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Written recipe: https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/the-best-korean-fried-chicken-at-home-recipe (serves 4, prep 20 min, cook 30 min; it says to make either the wings or the popcorn chicken, or both, from one batch of sauce, dredge and batter). The video makes both versions from that one batch, so the video is split into two recipe files (wings and nuggets) and the shared sauce, dredge, batter and frying lines are repeated in each. Sauce: tossed on the chicken and made in a bigger batch than goes on it (he calls it a big batch, uses it for both versions and says to use as much or as little as you like); no share is stated, so 50% of the batch is counted in each file (house rule 10; the full batch is about 2 2/3 cups). The garlic is strained out of the sauce (his recommendation), so it is not counted. Honey is listed as the alternative to rice syrup and not counted. Rice syrup uses a malt-syrup proxy and dark soy sauce uses regular soy sauce. Sweet soy sauce grams use our 1.25 g/ml estimate. Coatings: dry dredge 25% and wet batter 50% (house rule 3); because 1/3 cup of the dredge goes into the batter, each dredge ingredient counts at 27.6% (arithmetic in each line). The couple of tablespoons of batter flicked into the dredge for crunchy bits are ignored. Gram weights for starch, flour and MSG are the written recipe's. The 1-inch knob of ginger is our estimate of 10 g (his jerk chicken recipe weighs a 3-inch knob at 31 g). Frying oil: about 3 quarts in the video (the page says 2-3 quarts of canola or peanut oil; canola, named first, is used); the pot is excluded and absorbed oil is counted at 10% of the raw coated weight (house rule 2), using the as-bought weight. Times are the written recipe's hands-on prep and cook; the cure (at least 1 hour, ideally overnight) is not in prep_minutes (house rule 13). Wings: 2 lb whole wings from the written recipe (the video gives no weight). Green onions: 3 from the written recipe (garnish with an amount, so counted). Sesame seeds: garnish with no amount, not counted. Absorbed oil: raw weight is the 908 g wings plus 25 g of cure (7 g salt, 2 g sugar, 3 g MSG, 3 g pepper, 10 g ginger) plus 213.1 g of coating.

steps.text: Sauce: in a small saucepan, stir together the gochujang, rice syrup, dark soy sauce, vinegar, sweet soy sauce and ketchup. Boil over medium-high heat for 2-3 minutes to reduce.
Mince the garlic finely. With the heat completely off, stir it into the sauce (never boil it, or it turns bitter). Let it steep 5-10 minutes, then strain the garlic out.
Cure the whole wings: rub them thoroughly with the kosher salt, sugar, MSG, black pepper and grated ginger. Cover and refrigerate, ideally overnight.
Dry dredge: whisk the potato starch, flour, salt, sugar, MSG, garlic powder and white pepper together.
Wet batter: whisk 1/3 cup of the dredge with the baking powder, then whisk in the cold water. Optionally flick a couple of tablespoons of batter into the dredge to make crunchy bits.
Using one wet hand and one dry hand, dip each wing in the batter, then press it into the dredge until fully coated with no bare spots. Shake off the excess and set on a dry sheet tray.
First fry: heat about 3 quarts of oil to 325°F in a large pot. Fry the wings a few at a time for 8-10 minutes, until cooked through but still pale.
Second fry: raise the oil to 350°F (up to 375°F), skimming out loose bits of flour. Fry the wings again for 2-3 minutes until golden and very crisp. Drain on a rack.
While still hot, toss the wings in a bowl with as much sauce as you like until coated. Plate and garnish with toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onion.
